endorsements.quote: Therefore, before deploying any AI-enabled system, engaging in rigorous local validation efforts is paramount.

The creation and use of representative, well-balanced datasets play a pivotal role in facilitating algorithm development, fostering reproducibility in studies, and enabling local validation processes, all of which are important for reducing disparities among different subpopulations [ 8 , 11 ].

However, it is essential to implement appropriate legal and ethical measures to protect the confidentiality and security of data, regardless of whether it is considered personal or de-identified [ 11 ].

unlisted_practices: Establish partnerships among government agencies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers to develop more inclusive datasets representing rural and underserved populations.
Adhere to the FAIR principles (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability) and document datasets with comprehensive metadata.
Adopt standardized data formats such as DICOM and FHIR to enable interoperability among EHRs, imaging devices, and AI systems.
Participate in international open science initiatives and adopt global data-sharing standards while adhering to local privacy regulations.
Explore federated learning to enable collaborative AI training without sharing patient data, while mitigating adversarial attacks on model updates.
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among data scientists, healthcare professionals, and legal experts in AI development.
Explore innovative methods, such as mobile health and telemedicine, to collect diverse data from underrepresented regions.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary discussing data sharing, privacy, bias, and local validation under the Brazilian General Data Protection Law for AI in retinal imaging.
